scores.claim_text: 463 temperature-controlled warehouses (312 North America) ~81.9M sq ft / 9.8M pallet positions as of 3/31/2024.
scores.M_check: epa_frs.query_facilities (multi-state) — sector match: cold-storage ammonia-refrigeration facilities ARE EPA-regulated industrial sites.
scores.M_value: EPA FRS returns a large, geographically distributed Lineage cold-storage footprint: CA 29, TX 13, GA 12, IL 9, FL 8, PA 2 facilities named 'LINEAGE' / 'LINEAGE - <site>'. Sampled 6 states alone yield ~70+ registered facilities, consistent with a 312-North-America portfolio.
scores.interpretation: Independent EPA registry corroborates a very large, real, multi-state US cold-storage facility base. The facility-count claim is the strongest extraction for this name and the registry confirms it at scale. PASS.

scores.claim_text: Cold-storage warehouses use EPA/OSHA-regulated anhydrous-ammonia refrigeration with risk-management programs.
scores.M_check: epa_frs.query_facilities — presence in EPA FRS is itself evidence the sites are EPA-regulated industrial facilities (ammonia RMP / Clean Air Act 112(r) population).
scores.M_value: Lineage facilities appear directly in EPA's Facility Registry Service across every sampled state (IL 9, GA 12, WA Versacold 1, etc.). FRS registration is the regulatory hook the prospectus's environmental risk factor describes.
scores.interpretation: The regulatory-status claim (EPA-regulated ammonia-refrigeration facilities) is affirmatively confirmed: the company's sites are in the EPA registry exactly as the disclosure implies. PASS.

scores.claim_text: World's largest temperature-controlled warehousing company; largest automated portfolio with 81 automated facilities.
scores.M_check: epa_frs.query_facilities — registry confirms scale (the 'largest' superlative) but does not record automation status, so the '81 automated facilities' sub-claim and the global-ranking superlative are not registry-recordable.
scores.M_value: EPA FRS confirms a dominant US facility footprint (consistent with 'largest'), but no registry attests automation counts or a global #1 ranking; those are self-asserted competitive claims.
scores.interpretation: Scale portion is registry-corroborated; the 'largest globally' superlative and the 81-automated-facilities count are only partially verifiable (no registry covers automation/ranking). Partial corroboration with no contradiction -> MODERATE on the discriminative sub-claims, not a distress signal.

scores.claim_text: Serves >13,000 customers (household-name food retailers/processors); no single customer >3.3% of revenue; top 25 = ~32% of revenue; >60% of top-25 revenue investment-grade-rated.
scores.M_check: edgar_fts.query_fulltext — counterparty/external-validation test. (The prospectus deliberately ANONYMIZES its top-15 customer table to commodity categories, so no individual named customer is checkable; the testable proxy is whether independent SEC filers reference 'Lineage Logistics' as a real, widely-engaged counterparty.)
scores.M_value: EDGAR full-text search returns 110 third-party filing hits mentioning 'Lineage Logistics' (e.g. landlords/REITs such as W. P. Carey), confirming an extensive real counterparty footprint across the filing ecosystem.
scores.interpretation: The relationship reality and broad-base claim are strongly corroborated by independent filer references. The exact 13,000 count and the precise concentration percentages are self-disclosed and not directly registry-confirmable, but there is no contradiction and ample external validation that this is a genuine, large, diversified customer franchise. PASS, with the caveat that the specific count is UNVERIFIABLE in isolation.

scores.claim_text: Fifth-largest U.S. corporate / second-largest REIT producer of on-site solar and battery capacity (per 2022 SEIA Solar Means Business Report).
scores.M_check: No federal registry in the catalog records corporate on-site solar/battery rankings. EPA FRS confirms the facilities exist but does not attest a solar-production ranking; the cited source (SEIA report) is a third-party trade publication, not a queryable registry.
scores.M_value: No applicable registry. EPA FRS corroborates facility existence (where the solar would sit) but cannot confirm the ranking claim.
scores.interpretation: Ranking is sourced to a named third-party report but no available registry can independently confirm or refute it. Honestly scored UNVERIFIABLE rather than manufacturing severity; no contradiction observed.

scores.claim_text: $5.3B revenue and $(162.8)M net loss for TTM 3/31/2024; ~$10.7B total debt/debt-like obligations (historical), with disclosed covenant compliance as of 3/31/2024.
scores.M_check: Prospectus-internal disclosure quality assessment (financial-statement notes within the 424B4). going_concern_detector was attempted but its nearest filing post-dates the IPO cutoff, so it is NOT used as an outcome input; scoring rests on the prospectus's own honest disclosure.
scores.M_value: The filing transparently discloses the net loss, the full debt stack (Revolver/Term/CMBS/Senior Notes/finance leases), near-term CMBS maturities (ICE5 ~$1.3B due 11/2024 with extension option), and affirmative covenant compliance as of 3/31/2024. The loss and leverage are disclosed plainly, not masked.
scores.interpretation: This is an honesty-framework PASS: the negative facts (large net loss, heavy leverage, near-term maturities) are fully and prominently disclosed in the prospectus rather than obscured. The IPO use-of-proceeds is explicitly to de-lever (repay the $2.4B Delayed Draw Term Loan + revolver). Honest disclosure of impaired-but-real financials -> PASS under the honesty-alpha framework.
